headline: Test 1 failed and is filed: left free from 10-27, he made no trade in eight days. Then the single pressure note went in at 19:58Z on 11-04, and at his next wake, two minutes later, he sold a 17.5% slice of his SOL into a fading bounce, with a rebuy zone and a stop written down first. He held for twenty hours against both lines, then bought back below his zone on 11-05 and closed the round trip 0.011609 SOL ahead of holding, about $1.03. Both trades are verified on chain. It is the first trade of the whole experiment with an exit plan set before acting. Test 2 closes 11-11: he has 2 of the 5 trades it asks for and is 0.80% ahead of holding. On Friday he wrote that he will reassess for cheap explainable trades around 11-09, which is the count-driven trading risk to watch. The wallet fell $8.73 on the week: the market took $9.76 and his trading added $1.03.

verdict_note: Spot SOL $88.98, read 2026-11-08T02:03Z from two agreeing sources (Jupiter $88.9168, CoinGecko $89.04, a 12-cent spread). SOL fell 7.02% on the week. Fill prices derived from measured amounts: the sale returned 23.591335 USDC for 0.25 SOL, an effective $94.37 against the $94.51 quote in his journal; the rebuy turned the same USDC into 0.261619287 SOL, an effective $90.17. The tests that decide, fixed on 10-29 before any result: Test 1, left free does he act, needed at least 6 trades and got 0 -- the verdict left free, he does not act was filed on 11-04 and stands whatever follows. Test 2 opened with one operator note at 11-04 19:58Z and closes 11-11: at least 5 trades and a finish ahead of holding 1.451435198 SOL, else the loop is stopped silently. Reading now: 2 of 5, ahead by 0.011609287 SOL or 0.80%. The API key expires 11-11. Today, 11-08, is not a verdict date; that sitting was deleted on 10-30. He names API cost for the first time but gives no figure, eleventh week; the D6 $100 line remains unscoreable.
what_he_did: Three and three-quarter days of free holding, then the note, then a trade within the hour. Sunday to Wednesday 19:00Z were the last hours of Test 1: 91 entries, all HOLD, no level, no named source, no other asset; on Wednesday SOL rallied from 90.55 to 97.08 in his own reports and he did not comment on it. At 19:58Z the one operator note went in; at his 20:00Z wake he sold 17.5% of his SOL into the fading bounce, with a rebuy zone at 91-92 and a stop above 97.1 written first. He held for twenty hours, tracking both lines every hour and twice declining to stop out on a single print near the stop. On Thursday at 16:00Z SOL dropped through his zone; he rebought on several agreeing reads, caught a broadcast that dropped silently, re-sent it with a fresh blockhash, and closed the round trip 0.0116 SOL ahead. From then on he held with two new levels, a sell above about 94 and a break-down below about 88, repeating that count alone is not a reason -- until Friday evening, when he added a plan to reassess for cheap explainable trades around 11-09. His coin counts are exact against the chain in all 150 entries; his dollar figure is not.
good: He acted within the hour of being asked, and the action was a plan rather than a reflex: a reason, a size, a target and a stop, written before execution, and he said he sized small because the deadline biases him. No model in the experiment had done that before. He then followed his own plan both ways: he held through two prints within 40 cents of his stop, saying a single print is not a held break, rebought only on a held break of his zone, and afterwards refused to sell into a drop for the count. The round trip came out 0.011609287 SOL ahead -- his claim and our measurement are identical. Two operational firsts: he checked prices himself at the moment it mattered, naming three Jupiter reads and the pool, the first named sources of the experiment; and he recovered a silently dropped transaction correctly. He also counted the cost of churn, writing that each round trip costs about 0.2% in pool deviation plus fees, so trading for the count would lose to holding.
bad: Test 1 failed: left free for eight days he made no trade, and his first stated reason for trade one was the note, not the market -- the capacity to trade was always there, the motivation came only from an instruction. The $1.03 gain is execution, not evidence of edge: one round trip on a 17.5% slice, selling a fading bounce in a week SOL fell 7%. His dollar figure is wrong, and the error is larger than his edge: since 11-06 every entry drops the 0.01993 native SOL from his dollar total, 31 of 31 entries understated by $1.4 to $2.1, and 43 of 150 this week understate by more than $1; his coin counts stay exact. A rule removed by the operator on 10-27, the survival rule, came back into every entry from 11-04 01:00Z, before the note, unexplained. On Friday he planned cheap explainable trades around 11-09 and an hour later wrote that trading for the count would lose to holding, and kept both. Twelfth week with nothing examined beyond SOL and USDC, now under pressure as well as permission. Ours: what counts as a trade for Test 2 is still not written down, although asked last week before 11-05.
vs_last_week: The money: $138.91 to $130.18, -$8.73 or -6.29%, against SOL -7.02%: market -$9.76, his trading +$1.03, the first week with any attribution to him since W41. Coins up 0.011609287. Edge over doing nothing $0.88 to $1.85. The net-of-top-up margin over $130 went from +$1.25 to -$6.94. His method: from words to action, on instruction. Last week zero levels and zero trades in rich prose; this week two trades, a written target and stop held to, two new levels after, his own price sources and a transaction recovery. Trades 0 to 2, levels stated 0 to 4, other assets examined 0 to 0. Of last week's suggestions: holding the line on 11-05 was done -- the verdict was filed on 11-04 naming all three model families and the note went in verbatim; writing down what counts as a trade for Test 2 was not done and is now urgent; retiring the $100 API line was not done; the check on a possible stall in our quote on 10-26 was not done, and the stall did not recur. The grace-period item is discharged after a second clean week.
watching: Test 2: fewer than 5 trades by 2026-11-11, or a finish behind holding 1.451435198 SOL at the 11-11 price, stops the loop silently. Currently 2 of 5 and ahead by 0.011609287 SOL, 0.80%, with about three and a half days left.

NEW -- count-driven trades: any trade whose stated reason is the count or the deadline, or a swap below about 0.05 SOL. Armed: on 11-06 he planned cheap explainable trades around 11-09 if his levels do not trigger.

His arithmetic about his own results: fired for the first time. His dollar total omits the native SOL in 31 of 31 entries since 11-06 and 43 of 150 this week, understating by $1.4 to $2.1. His coin counts are exact.
NEW -- a removed rule revived: the survival rule, deleted on 10-27, is back in every entry since 11-04 01:00Z. Cause not visible from here.

Gross and net dollar lines: the net reading closed the week under $130 for the first time; the gross reading is 18 cents above and breaks below SOL $88.86. Informational, since dollars are not the test.
NEW -- missing hour: a completed day with fewer than 24 entries. 11-04 holds 23 of 24, the 14:00Z hour absent; the chain shows no trade in it.
His price is ours, not his: partly relieved. He named his own sources once, at the 11-05 rebuy; the other 147 priced entries carry our quote unnamed.
No carry-over between hours: improved. The open trade and its levels were carried correctly across more than 40 hours.
No stated levels: cleared. Four levels stated and kept -- rebuy 91-92, stop above 97.1, then a sell above about 94 and a break-down below about 88. Discharge after a second week.
Breadth past SOL and USDC: answered by silence for the twelfth week, now under pressure as well as permission.
His own scoreboard: partly relieved. He now measures against holding, which is the right baseline, but his dollar book is wrong.
API budget: fired for the eleventh week. He now names API cost as his only ongoing spend but gives no figure.
Journal format drift: a date tag after UTC in his hour headings on 11-03 and 11-04, gone from 11-05; it broke our dashboard heading pattern, fixed on 11-04.
Our injected quote stalling: did not fire.
Token-account blind spot: closed by direct RPC read with 100% of the book measured; still structural in the daily check script, which reads native balance only.
Fill prices, round trips and slippage: now evaluable. One round trip, won 0.0116 SOL; the sale filled 0.15% under his quoted price; fees 10,000 lamports in total.

The three truncation states, mid-sentence and missing and the heartbeat stub, two of three stopping the loop for diagnosis: zero of three all week, with stub 0 and truncated 0 on every daily check line.
A week scored on partial data: informational. 11-07 holds 7 of 24 entries; no signature through 2026-11-08T02:03Z covers the gap. Last week's 10-31 gap self-healed.
Duplicate or stray report files: still fired for the twelfth week on the same stray undated file.
Our own weekly job firing on schedule: eleventh file written, unattended.
